sn14.11:1.4: This set of seven offers a unique perspective on familiar meditations.
sn14.11:3.1: Whereas “luminosity” (_ābhā_) is often the radiance of the sun and moon, or the light cast by a flame, here it is the illumination that appears in deep meditation.
sn14.11:3.2: “Beauty” (_subha_) is the focus of wholly pure and exalted meditations, such as the meditation on love, or the sight of a pure brilliant color like the sky ([mn77:22.6]()). It contrasts with the meditation on “ugliness”, such as the parts of the body or a decomposing corpse. At [an6.41:2.7](), Sāriputta explains that an accomplished meditator could see a tree as nothing but beauty or nothing but ugliness, since both of those elements are present in it.
